30305-dp:
Arthur Dekker Savage tells DP, illustrated by Paul Orban, a short tale of a perfection that breeds boredom. Once upon a time life was perfection, the tagline says, with government making sure citizens were supplied with every comfort and pleasure, but sometimes perfection breeds boredom. Allen Kinderwood slows his pace so his forelock will quit bobbing, a dark lock supposed to form a peaked crest above handsome features.

No matter how he combs it and applies lusto-set, it bobs if he walks too fast. Though it should not matter now, since he is not looking for a woman tonight. His appointment with the Social Adjustment counsellors comes tomorrow morning. A Departure Permit should be his tomorrow, and no DP petition, so far as he knows, has ever been refused. He spends his last night in the park of C Sector, among crowds, trying to settle his thoughts.
